title: Good Will Hunting · The park bench
description: The complete supplied park conversation, with physical Sean and Will voices, original music and ambience, pond, swans, trees, a wooden bench and the quiet walk-away ending.

characters.name: Sean Maguire
characters.role: Your move, chief · CHIMERA physical voice

characters.name: Will Hunting
characters.role: Listening on the park bench · CHIMERA physical voice

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: So what's this?

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: A Taster's Choice moment between guys?

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: This is really nice.

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: You got a thing for swans? Is this like a fetish?

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: It's something like maybe we need to devote some time to?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Thought about what you said to me the other day.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: About my painting.

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: Huh?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I stayed up half the night thinking about it.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Something occurred to me.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I fell into a deep peaceful sleep.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: and I haven't thought about you since.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You know what occurred to me?

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: No.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You're just a kid.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You don't have the faintest idea of what you're talking about.

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: Why, thank you.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: It's all right.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You've never been out of Boston?

cues.speaker: will
cues.text: Nope.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: So if I asked you about art, you'd probably give me the skinny on every art book ever written.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Michelangelo.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You know a lot about him.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Life's work, political aspirations, him and the pope,

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: sexual orientation, the whole works, right?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I bet you can't tell me what it smells like in the Sistine Chapel.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You never actually stood there and looked up at that beautiful ceiling.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I've seen that.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: If I ask you about women, you'd probably give me a syllabus of your personal favorites.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You may have even been laid a few times.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: But you can't tell me what it feels like to wake up next to a woman and feel truly happy.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You're a tough kid.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: When I ask you about war, you'd probably throw Shakespeare at me, right?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Once more into the breach, dear friends.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: But you've never been near one.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You've never held your best friend's head in your lap and watched him gasp his last breath, looking to you for help.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: When I ask you about love,

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: you'd probably quote me a sonnet.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: But you've never looked at a woman and been totally vulnerable,

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: known someone that could level you with her eyes,

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Feeling like God put an angel on Earth just for you.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Who could rescue you from the depths of hell.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: And you wouldn't know what it's like to be her angel.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: To have that love for her be there forever.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Through anything.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Through cancer.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: And you wouldn't know about sleeping sitting up in a hospital room for two months holding her hand.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Because the doctors could see in your eyes that the terms visiting hours don't apply to you.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You don't know about real loss, because that only occurs when you love something more than you love yourself.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I doubt you've ever dared to love anybody that much.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I look at you, I don't see an intelligent, confident man.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I see a cocky, scared, shitless kid.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: But you're a genius, Will. No one denies that.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: No one could possibly understand the depths of you.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: But you presume to know everything about me because you saw a painting of mine and you ripped my fucking life apart.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You're an orphan, right?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Do you think I'd know the first thing about how hard your life has been?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: How you feel, who you are.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Because I read Oliver Twist.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Does that encapsulate you?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Personally, I don't give a shit about all that because you know what?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I can't learn anything from you.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I can't read in some fucking book.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Unless you want to talk about you, who you are.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: And I'm fascinated.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: I'm in, but you don't want to do that, do you, sport?

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: You're terrified of what you might say.

cues.speaker: sean
cues.text: Your move, chief.
